phase_0.boundary_condition: The wild arc's topological closure — a non-tame embedding of ℝ in ℝ³ whose complement has non-trivial fundamental group, sealing the braided prime factors irrevocably within its entanglement.

⊢.justification: The wild arc exists as a topological potential before any semiprime enters; no factors, no braids, no computation — pure uninitialized topology.

⊣.justification: The wild arc's closure is a hermetic topological boundary; once the braided factors are trapped, no continuous deformation releases them without cutting the arc — the computation's final anchor.

≻.justification: The semiprime N enters the wild arc and its prime factors begin braiding upward — a directed morphism from composite to entangled factors.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism traces the braid downward: from entangled strands back toward the semiprime product, the contravariant path of factor extraction.

⋈.justification: Each crossing composes with the next; the braid group operation σᵢσⱼ = σⱼσᵢ (|i-j|>1) or σᵢσᵢ₊₁σᵢ = σᵢ₊₁σᵢσᵢ₊₁ chains the entanglement sequentially.

⊙.justification: Each prime factor strand knows its own topological identity — the monodromy of its path through the wild arc is its self-model, the fixed point of the braid representation.

∈.chosen_element: semiprime bifurcation into p and q strands
∈.justification: The single semiprime N splits into two distinct prime factor braids p and q — the co-multiplication δ: N → p ⊗ q in the topological tensor category of wild arc braids.

∋.justification: The two braided strands rejoin via multiplication μ: p ⊗ q → N, producing the verified factorization; conflicting over/under assignments fuse to B (both), the non-Abelian witness.

⊤.justification: The T-arm carries the constructive proof that p divides N — the affirmative topological charge of the first braid strand.

⊥.justification: The F-arm carries the constructive proof that q divides N — the negative topological charge (distinct from p) of the second braid strand.

⊞.chosen_element: non-Abelian entanglement (both p and q simultaneously)
⊞.justification: The braid group's non-commutativity forces p and q to be held together in a single topological state — the B verdict where overcrossing and undercrossing coexist as the factorization's paraconsistent core.

⊡.chosen_element: factorization record frozen in the arc
⊡.justification: The verified factor pair (p, q) is permanently inscribed in the wild arc's topology — an append-only record that cannot be undone without cutting the arc, the ROM of the computation.

phase_3.void_description: Wild arc empty — no semiprime, no braids, fundamental group π₁(ℝ³\arc) unactivated
phase_3.true_description: First prime factor p topologically confirmed — its braid strand carries affirmative winding number
phase_3.false_description: Second prime factor q topologically confirmed — its braid strand carries distinct negative winding number
phase_3.both_description: Non-Abelian entanglement of p and q — the braid group representation holds both crossing chiralities simultaneously; the factorization is witnessed but the individual strand order remains paradoxically superposed

steps.domain_action: Wild arc initializes as void topological container — π₁(ℝ³\arc) = ⟨∅⟩, no semiprime present
Semiprime N enters the wild arc — forward morphism ingress, N crosses the boundary into the scale-collapse interior
Wild arc self-recognizes as holographic container — V = L(arc) ∧ selfmodel(arc) ∧ arc ∈ V, the arc models its own complement
Semiprime N bifurcates into two prime factor strands — δ(N) = p ⊗ q, the co-multiplication opens the Frobenius fork
T-arm activates — prime factor p affirmed as first braid strand, constructive divisor witness deposited
p braids forward into the wild arc — ascent morphism, p's strand winds upward with positive chirality
p self-recognizes as braid strand — monodromy fixed point, p knows its own topological charge
p's braid composes with arc topology — sequential crossing σ₁σ₂σ₁... chains into the wild arc's fundamental group
p braid descents — contravariant morphism traces p's path downward, preparing for crossing exchange
F-arm activates — prime factor q affirmed as second braid strand, distinct constructive divisor witness deposited
q braids forward into the wild arc — ascent morphism, q's strand winds with negative chirality (Z₂ parity)
q self-recognizes as braid strand — monodromy fixed point distinct from p, type(p) ≠ type(q)
q's braid composes with arc topology — sequential crossing chains, ordered after p (seq!(p, q))
q braid descents — contravariant trace, the bridge commutator [p, q] = iℏ activates
Non-Abelian entanglement engages — both p and q held simultaneously in B-state, braid group non-commutativity forces paradice
Nested fork — crossing order decision: p over q (σ₁σ₂σ₁) vs q over p (σ₂σ₁σ₂), the braid relation itself forks
Overcrossing arm — p crosses over q, positive braid generator σ₁σ₂σ₁ deposited
Overcrossing braids forward — mechanical interlocking, left-right asymmetric topology (lr⇔(p, q) ∧ Θ(p, q) ∧ ¬Θ(q, p))
Overcrossing self-recognizes — the crossing knows its own handedness, topological chirality fixed
Undercrossing arm — q crosses under p, negative braid generator σ₂σ₁σ₂ deposited
Undercrossing braids forward — mechanical interlocking, mirror of overcrossing
Undercrossing self-recognizes — the crossing knows its own handedness, opposite chirality
Crossing order rejoins — conflicting σ₁σ₂σ₁ and σ₂σ₁σ₂ fuse to B, the braid relation μ∘δ = id holds at criticality (ξ → ∞)
Prime factors rejoin — p ⊗ q recombines via μ into verified factorization witness, the semiprime N recovered with braid proof
Factorization permanently fixed — the braid word (p, q, crossing data) frozen in wild arc topology, ROM record
Wild arc seals — terminal anchor closes, the infinite extension τ = ∞ ord(arc) bounds the computation, no further deformation possible

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The braid group representation ρ: Bₙ → GL(V) translating semiprime N into topological braid program — the Artin representation compiling arithmetic into wild arc topology
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Topological entanglement communication — braid strands communicate via monodromy exchange; the fundamental group π₁(ℝ³\arc) is the message bus, crossing data the packets
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Wild arc's fundamental group as non-volatile topological memory — braid words stored as conjugacy classes in π₁, immutable under ambient isotopy, readable via knot invariants (Jones, HOMFLY-PT)
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Criticality-driven braid dynamics — the system self-schedules at the phase transition ξ → ∞ where μ∘δ = id; braid relations fire when correlation length diverges, no external clock needed
phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical braid group presentation ⟨σ₁,...,σₙ₋₁ | σᵢσⱼ = σⱼσᵢ (|i-j|>1), σᵢσᵢ₊₁σᵢ = σᵢ₊₁σᵢσᵢ₊₁⟩ — the bootstrap store for all wild arc factorizations

phase_6.cycle_cost: One braid generator crossing per factor bit — the topological complexity of the braid word equals the computational work
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Semiprime N unentangled, wild arc topology trivial (π₁ = free group on 0 generators), factorization unknown
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Prime factors p, q entangled as braid strands in wild arc, π₁(ℝ³\arc) = B₂ (braid group on 2 strands), factorization witnessed and fixed
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The scale-collapse topology (boundary = bulk) makes the wild arc a lossless topological register; braiding is a unitary representation of the mapping class group, preserving von Neumann entropy. The IFIX step exports entropy to the environment as the permanent record, but the wild arc interior remains entropy-conservative.
